title: Classroom Welcome Mat: Size, Price and Personalization Guide
meta_description: Chillgen classroom welcome mats come in 3 door sizes, from $21.90 blank or $28.90 personalized. Measure your door, then check this size and price table.
body_html:
A Chillgen classroom welcome mat starts at $21.90 blank or $28.90 personalized. Which one fits depends on three things: how wide your doorway is, whether you want your name on it, and whether you also need a rug the kids can sit on.

Contents

  1. What size classroom welcome mat fits your doorway?
  2. Are personalized school mats worth it over a blank mat?
  3. Doormat or sit-on rug? The comparison table
  4. Math rug, composition rug or feelings wheel rug: which design?
  5. How big a rug does your group need?
  6. A worked example: one classroom, start to finish
  7. What to check on the product page before you order

What size classroom welcome mat fits your doorway?

Classroom doormats come in three sizes. Each has a metric equivalent, which helps if your school measures in centimeters:

  • 24"x16" (40x60 cm): from $21.90
  • 32"x20" (50x80 cm): from $30.90
  • 36"x24" (60x90 cm): from $34.90

Some listings price the same sizes differently:

  • 24"x16": from $25.89
  • 32"x20": from $27.89
  • 36"x24": from $33.89

Check the price on the listing you're actually buying from, not the one in a search result.

The first number is the width, and that's the one that matters at a door. Measure the inside of the door frame, hinge side to latch side, at floor level. A mat a little narrower than the opening sits flat and doesn't catch on the frame. A mat wider than the opening only works out in the hallway, so ask whether your school allows anything in the corridor before you count on that.

The second number is depth, meaning how far the mat runs into the room or hallway. If your door swings inward, measure the gap between the bottom of the door and the floor, because a thick mat can stop the door opening fully. Mat thickness isn't published in the figures this page draws on. Compare your gap with the product page before you order.

What to check

  • Door opening width at floor level, in inches.
  • Which way the door swings, and the gap under it.
  • Whether the mat goes inside the room or in the hallway, and what your school allows.
  • The price on the exact listing, since the same size can start at a different price elsewhere.

Are personalized school mats worth it over a blank mat?

You can order a doormat two ways: Blank Doormat, No Custom from $21.90, or Customized Doormat from $28.90. Personalization is the main reason teachers choose these over a plain mat. Of the 136 products in the range, 114 list personalization on the product page.

A name pays off if you keep the same classroom for years, or if you move schools and take your things with you. A mat that says "Ms. Rivera's Room" labels the room for substitutes, visiting parents and new students in the first week. A blank mat makes more sense if you share a room, expect to be moved, or want a design you can pass on to a colleague.

Some personalized designs start at $25.89 at 24"x16". They include the Dinosaur Classroom Welcome Mat and the School Doodle Welcome Mat. That's below the "Customized Doormat" starting price, so pricing clearly varies by listing. Compare the final price after you've picked your options.

Decide on the exact wording before you type anything in. A name, a grade level and a room number are the usual pieces. Shorter text is easier to read from across a hallway.

What to check

  • Whether you'll be in this room next year.
  • The exact wording and spelling, including the title you use (Mr., Ms., Mx., Dr.).
  • The final price after you pick a size and personalization, not the starting price.
  • How the name looks in the preview at your chosen size, if the listing shows one.

What to check

Math rug, composition rug or feelings wheel rug: which design?

Most design searches come down to three themes. The names don't always tell you whether you're looking at a doormat or a floor rug.

Math rug. The Math Teacher Classroom Mat is a personalized doormat that starts at $25.89. It marks the room as a math room at the door. It isn't a teaching rug that kids sit on and count from. For a math activity rug, look at the square and rectangular rugs in the collection.

Composition rug. The Black Emotion Classroom Rug with Feel Can Prompts is listed as a custom composition notebook rug with feelings artwork. It starts at $31.90, the same figure as the 2x2 ft (XS, 1 kid) size, so the entry price fits one child at a time.

Feelings wheel rug. The How Are You Feeling Classroom Rug is listed as a round feelings wheel rug and starts at $30.89. A rug like this suits a daily check-in spot, where a child points to how they feel.

A fourth option is the Affirmation Pencil Classroom Mat, a personalized doormat from $25.89. Like the math mat, it goes at the door, not on the floor.

To choose, ask what the design is for. A door design sets the tone as kids walk in. A feelings design gets used every day, so it needs a spot where one or two children can sit without being in the way.

What to check

  • Whether the design is a doormat or a floor rug.
  • That the size matches how many kids will use it at once.
  • That the colors work with the rest of the room.
  • Any wording printed on the design, read in full before you order.

How big a rug does your group need?

The square rugs are sized by how many children they hold, which is often more useful than feet:

  • 1.6x1.6 ft, XXS (super small): from $24.90
  • 2x2 ft, XS (1 kid): from $31.90
  • 3x3 ft, S (2 kids): from $49.90
  • 4x4 ft, M (3 to 4 kids): price shown on the listing
  • 5x5 ft, L (5 to 7 kids): price shown on the listing
  • 6x6 ft, XL (8 to 12 kids): price shown on the listing

The kid counts are the seller's labels. Assume they mean children sitting close together, not each with room to spread out. Size for the largest number of children who'll use the spot at once, not the average. If your guided reading group is sometimes five and sometimes seven, plan for seven.

For a whole class, look at the rectangular sizes, which run from 24"x36" up to 120"x144". Measure the clear floor area first: the space left once desks, shelves and walkways are accounted for. Mark the corners with painter's tape and have the children sit inside it once. That tells you more than any label.

What to check

  • The largest number of children who'll sit on it at once.
  • The clear floor space, taped out on the floor.
  • How close it sits to doors and walkways, so nobody has to cut across it.
  • The price at your size, since only the three smallest square sizes have starting prices published here.

A worked example: one classroom, start to finish

Every figure in this example is made up to show the process. It isn't a customer story.

A second-grade teacher wants two things: a personalized mat at the door, and a rug for a reading corner where up to six children sit at once.

The door. They measure the opening at 36 inches. A 36"x24" mat would match the frame exactly and leave no clearance. They choose the 32"x20" size instead, which leaves a gap on both sides. They'll keep the room next year, so they pick Customized Doormat. They type the wording once, "Welcome to Mr. Okafor's Class", and check the spelling twice.

The corner. Six children is more than the 4x4 ft M rug holds (3 to 4 kids), so they look at the 5x5 ft L rug (5 to 7 kids). They tape a 5x5 ft square on the floor, and it fits with a walkway still clear. They want the feelings theme, so before going further they check whether the round feelings wheel rug comes in the size they taped out.

The budget. The doormat's price depends on the listing and size, so they read it in the cart rather than from a search result. The 5x5 ft price isn't published in the figures here either. They add both items, confirm the sizes and wording, and only then compare the total with what they planned to spend.

What to check on the product page before you order

Features vary by product, and the collection doesn't print the same claims on every listing. Here's how often each feature is stated across the 136 products:

Feature as stated on the product pageListings that state it
"Non-slip neoprene rubber backing for stability"114 of 136
"Supports personalization with custom sizes"114 of 136
"Soft and comfortable memory foam surface"50 of 136
"Soft and comfortable low pile surface"35 of 136
"Easy to clean and maintain"34 of 136

Backing matters most at a door, where the mat gets walked on all day. 22 of the 136 listings don't state the non-slip backing, so look for that line on the specific product.

Memory foam and low pile are two different surfaces, and each listing says which one it uses. Foam suits a spot where children sit. Low pile is flatter, which helps when a door has to swing over it. Only 34 listings mention easy cleaning, and the figures here don't include care instructions. If a rug is headed for a busy corner, find out how to clean it before you order.

What to check

  • Whether the listing states the non-slip neoprene backing.
  • Whether the surface is memory foam or low pile, and which one your spot needs.
  • Care instructions, especially for rugs children sit on.
  • Size, personalization and tapestry choices, all confirmed in the cart.
